title: Net Tangible Assets Requirement
description: The issuer must have net tangible assets of at least ₹3 crore in each of the preceding three full years (of twelve months each). Not more than 50% of the net tangible assets shall be monetary assets. If monetary assets exceed 50%, the issuer must have made firm commitments to deploy the excess monetary assets in its business or the project proposed to be funded from the IPO. This restriction on monetary assets does not apply if the IPO is entirely an Offer for Sale.

title: Monetary Assets Limit in NTA
description: Not more than 50% of the net tangible assets in each of the preceding three full years shall be held as monetary assets (cash and bank balances). If monetary assets exceed 50%, the company must have made firm commitments to deploy them in its business/projects. This restriction does not apply if the IPO is entirely an Offer for Sale (OFS).

title: Operating Profit Track Record
description: The issuer must have an average pre-tax operating profit (profit before tax excluding extraordinary and non-recurring items) of at least ₹15 crore calculated over the three most profitable years out of the immediately preceding five years. Each of those three years must show a positive operating profit.

title: Minimum Net Worth
description: The issuer must have a net worth of at least ₹1 crore in each of the preceding three full years (of twelve months each). Net worth is calculated as per the Companies Act, 2013 — paid-up share capital plus all reserves created out of profits and securities premium account, minus accumulated losses, deferred expenditure, and miscellaneous expenditure.

title: Issue Size vs Pre-Issue Net Worth
description: The aggregate of the proposed issue size (fresh issue component only) and all previous issues made in the same financial year shall not exceed five times the pre-issue net worth of the company as per the audited balance sheet of the preceding financial year.

title: Name Change Revenue Requirement
description: If the issuer has changed its name within the last one year, at least 50% of the revenue for the preceding one full year must have been earned from the activity suggested by the new name. This ensures companies do not rename themselves to benefit from trending sectors without actual business operations in that area.

title: QIB Route Allocation
description: If the issuer does not satisfy the conditions under Regulation 6(1) (Profitability Route), it may still make an IPO provided: (a) the issue is made only through the book-building process, and (b) the issuer undertakes to allot at least 75% of the net offer to Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs). If 75% QIB allocation is not achieved, the full subscription amount must be refunded.

title: SEBI Debarment Check
description: The issuer, its promoters, promoter group members, directors, and selling shareholders must not be debarred from accessing the capital market by SEBI at the time of filing the offer document. Any existing SEBI order debarring any of these parties renders the company ineligible for an IPO.

title: Wilful Defaulter Status
description: Neither the issuer nor any of its promoters or directors shall be a wilful defaulter as declared by any bank or financial institution. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) maintains guidelines on the classification of wilful defaulters. Companies with promoters or directors tagged as wilful defaulters are barred from accessing the capital market.

title: Fugitive Economic Offender Check
description: No promoter or director of the issuer shall be a fugitive economic offender as defined under the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018. A company with a promoter or director declared a fugitive economic offender is absolutely barred from making a public issue.

title: Outstanding Convertible Securities
description: The issuer shall not have any outstanding convertible securities or any other right which would entitle any person any option to receive equity shares of the issuer, except employee stock options (ESOPs) granted under an ESOP scheme, or fully paid-up convertible securities that have been converted prior to filing. All convertible instruments must be resolved before the DRHP filing.

regulation: SEBI LODR Regulation 17 / Companies Act 2013 Sec 149
title: Board Independence Requirement
description: The board of directors must have an optimum combination of executive and non-executive directors. At least one-third of the board must comprise Independent Directors. If the Chairperson is an executive director, a promoter, or related to a promoter, then at least one-half (50%) of the board must be Independent Directors. Independent directors must meet the criteria under Section 149(6) of the Companies Act, 2013.

regulation: SEBI LODR Regulation 17(1)(a) / Companies Act 2013 Sec 149(1)
title: Woman Director Requirement
description: The board of directors must include at least one woman director. This is a mandatory requirement under both the Companies Act, 2013 and SEBI LODR Regulations. For top listed entities by market capitalization, there must be at least one independent woman director.

regulation: SEBI LODR Regulation 18 / Companies Act 2013 Sec 177
title: Audit Committee Constitution
description: The issuer must have a qualified Audit Committee constituted before filing the DRHP. Requirements: (1) Minimum 3 directors as members, (2) Two-thirds majority must be Independent Directors, (3) Chairperson must be an Independent Director, (4) All members must be financially literate, (5) At least one member must have accounting or financial management expertise (e.g., CA, CFO).

regulation: SEBI LODR Regulation 19 / Companies Act 2013 Sec 178
title: Nomination & Remuneration Committee
description: The Nomination and Remuneration Committee (NRC) must be constituted with: (1) At least three non-executive directors, (2) At least two-thirds of the members being Independent Directors, (3) Chairperson being an Independent Director. The committee formulates criteria for board appointments, recommends remuneration policies, and evaluates board performance.

regulation: SEBI LODR Regulation 20 / Companies Act 2013 Sec 178(5)
title: Stakeholders Relationship Committee
description: The Stakeholders Relationship Committee (SRC) must be constituted to consider and resolve grievances of security holders. It should be chaired by a non-executive director and include members with experience in investor relations and grievance redressal mechanisms.

title: Compliance Officer Appointment
description: A qualified Company Secretary (CS) must be appointed as the Compliance Officer of the company. The Compliance Officer is responsible for ensuring compliance with SEBI regulations, listing requirements, and handling all regulatory correspondence. This appointment must be made before filing the DRHP.

title: Minimum Promoter Contribution
description: Promoters of the issuer must contribute a minimum of 20% of the post-issue equity share capital. This contribution ensures that promoters have adequate skin in the game and are committed to the company's long-term performance post-listing. The shares contributed towards MPC must be from the promoter's existing holding or new subscription.

title: Lock-in of Minimum Promoter Contribution
description: The minimum promoter contribution (20% of post-issue capital) shall be locked-in for a period of 18 months from the date of allotment in the IPO. During this lock-in period, promoters cannot sell, transfer, pledge, or otherwise dispose of these shares. This is a mandatory post-listing compliance requirement that must be disclosed in the offer document.

title: Lock-in of Excess Promoter Holding
description: Promoter shareholding in excess of the minimum promoter contribution (i.e., shares held above 20% of post-issue capital) shall be locked-in for a period of 6 months from the date of allotment in the IPO. This applies to all shares held by the promoter and promoter group that are not part of the MPC.

title: Public Limited Company Status
description: The issuer must be a Public Limited Company to be eligible for an IPO. If the entity is currently a Private Limited Company or LLP, it must be converted to a Public Limited Company before filing the DRHP. Conversion involves alteration of the Memorandum of Association (MoA), Articles of Association (AoA), increasing minimum directors to 3, and meeting all public company requirements.

regulation: SEBI ICDR Schedule VI Part A
title: Restated Financial Statements
description: The issuer must prepare restated financial statements for the last three financial years (plus stub period if applicable) in compliance with Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS). These financial statements must be audited by an auditor who has been peer-reviewed by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI). The restated financials form the basis for all financial eligibility checks.
